title: Dying in prison. Exploration of the experiences and needs of prisoners and the reality of care provision
summary:
Background: A diagnosis of an incurable, life-limiting illness can affect anyone in any situation in life, including while serving a prison sentence. In Germany, dying prisoners are then usually released from prison early, provided that public safety is not endangered. However, there are also individual cases in which prisoners are expected to die in prison in the longer term. Dealing with seriously ill and dying prisoners poses particular challenges and entails a great deal of responsibility. This is solely due to the vulnerability of the prisoner population, which is exacerbated at the end of life. Until now, the issue of care for the seriously ill and dying in the German prison system has received little attention in an academic context.
Research questions: What experiences, needs, and wishes do seriously ill and dying prisoners or released prisoners have with regard to care in prison? What is the reality of care for seriously ill and dying prisoners? To what extent are there deficits or previously unmet needs in the area of palliative care in prison?
Method: An exploratory, qualitative interview study will be conducted. The interviewees will be prisoners/released prisoners with a serious, life-limiting illness, caregivers within the prison system, and caregivers outside the prison system.

interventions.name: One-time, narrative interviews with incarcerated or released individuals with a serious, life-limiting illness
One-time, guided interviews with caregivers within the prison system
One-time, guided interviews with caregivers outside the prison system

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
A) Prisoners and released prisoners who have been diagnosed with an incurable, progressive, life-limiting illness while in prison (in open or closed detention)
B) Internal caregivers: employees of a prison in Lower Saxony who have already been involved in caring for seriously ill and dying prisoners
C) External caregivers: employees of palliative care services who have already been involved in the care of seriously ill and dying prisoners in Lower Saxony
Exclusion criteria:
Cognitive impairments (e.g., dementia), insufficient knowledge of German
Discontinuation criterion: significant emotional stress during the interview
